top_five.text: An unprecedented Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has killed over 2,700 people and infected more than 5,700, outstripping regional containment capabilities.

Devastating flash floods along the Nepal-China border have killed hundreds of people and left over 1,000 missing, with a rapidly filling upstream lake threatening further catastrophic outburst flooding.
The confirmed death toll from Venezuela's major earthquakes has risen to 6,509, with more than 16,700 people injured and over 1,500 missing.
Direct military conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran intensified with fresh airstrikes on Tehran following the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader.
An armed gang assault in Kenscoff, Haiti, killed at least 47 people—including displaced civilians sheltering in a church—and resulted in the abduction of over 50 residents.

top_story.quote: A rapidly expanding Ebola outbreak driven by the Bundibugyo strain in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has infected over 5,700 people and claimed more than 2,700 lives, outpacing containment capacity.
top_story.label: AFRICA — DRC Ebola Outbreak

Middle East.headline: Middle East — US, Israel, and Iran Launch Fresh Airstrikes in Expanding Regional Conflict
Middle East.body: Direct military conflict involving the United States, Israel, and Iran entered its eighth day with renewed airstrikes and drone attacks targeting multiple locations, including Tehran. The escalation follows a joint US-Israeli strike that killed Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and senior commanders, triggering retaliatory attacks from Tehran. Concurrently, the US administration approved a 151 million dollar arms sale to Israel.

Middle East.headline: Lebanon — Israeli Shelling and Airstrikes Hit Southern Towns
Middle East.body: Israeli forces conducted airstrikes and artillery shelling across southern Lebanon, striking the towns of Al-Mansouri, Sarbein, Beit Lif, and the Wadi Zibqin area. Lebanese official media reported that Israeli drones dropped explosive canisters on residential homes in Al-Mansouri, while warplanes carried out multiple bombing runs. The attacks mark continued violations of the regional ceasefire agreement.

Middle East.headline: Democratic Republic of the Congo — Funding Allocated for Ebola Vaccine Development Amid Outbreak
Middle East.body: The Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations committed up to 16.5 million dollars to Egyptian drugmaker Minapharm to advance a candidate vaccine into clinical trials against the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola. The funding aims to combat an ongoing Ebola outbreak concentrated in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, which has caused over 2,700 deaths. The event marks the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record.

Middle East.headline: Nepal — Severe Flash Floods Kill Over 350 People Along Border
Middle East.body: Flash flooding near the Nepal-Tibet border killed more than 350 people and left nearly 1,400 missing, mostly tourists. Rising water levels at a lake formed by the disaster prompted authorities to warn of potential bursts, threatening further hazards. Flooding destroyed trees and electricity infrastructure, disrupting transport and complicating emergency responses along key travel routes.

Americas.headline: Haiti — Gang Massacre and Mass Abduction in Kenscoff
Americas.body: A violent attack by armed gangs in Kenscoff, near Port-au-Prince, killed at least 47 people and led to the abduction of dozens of residents, according to United Nations and international reports. Victims included displaced civilians who were executed inside a church compound where they were seeking shelter. At least 22 people were injured, and thousands of residents fled the town. Gang leader Izo 2 threatened to kill the hostages if security operations were launched against his group. UN Secretary-General António Guterres condemned the assault, emphasizing the worsening security situation in Haiti and calling for urgent international security support.

Americas.headline: Venezuela — Earthquake Death Toll Rises Above 6,500
Americas.body: The death toll from two major earthquakes that struck Venezuela on June 24 has risen to 6,509 following the confirmation of 71 additional fatalities, according to National Assembly President Jorge Rodríguez. Officials reported that 16,740 people have been injured during the disaster. In La Guaira state, the region hardest hit by casualties and destruction, Governor José Alejandro Terán confirmed that 1,579 individuals remain missing. Emergency responses and search operations continue as authorities assess the full scale of casualties and structural losses.

Americas.headline: Colombia — 5.1-Magnitude Earthquake Prompts Evacuations
Americas.body: A 5.1-magnitude earthquake struck Santander department in northeastern Colombia on Wednesday, with its epicenter located in Los Santos at a depth of 149 kilometers, according to the Colombian Geological Survey. The tremor caused shaking across central and northeastern regions, prompting precautionary evacuations in Bogotá and Bucaramanga. The seismic event occurred 16 days after a separate 7.4-magnitude earthquake caused over 300 fatalities in the country. No immediate casualties or significant structural damages were reported following Wednesday's earthquake.
verified_figures: more than 300 killed in previous 7.4-magnitude earthquake

Africa.headline: DR Congo — Ebola Outbreak and Displacement Crisis Escalation
Africa.body: An Ebola epidemic in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, driven by the Bundibugyo strain, has become the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak on record. UN Secretary-General António Guterres warned the virus is expanding faster than containment capabilities. Health authorities report at least 5,713 confirmed cases and 2,744 deaths, with over 300 fatalities recorded in a single week. Local experts caution the true scale may be three times higher due to out-of-facility deaths. The public health emergency is severely compounding insecurity in Ituri and surrounding regions, where persistent conflict has forced over 16,400 Congolese to flee into neighboring countries since January, overwhelming host communities and essential services.
verified_figures: 317 deaths reported in a single week
More than 16,400 refugees fled to neighbouring countries since January

Africa.headline: Somalia — Humanitarian Preparedness for Climate Shocks and Displacement
Africa.body: The Somali Disaster Management Agency met with the Norwegian Refugee Council in Mogadishu to review response strategies for compounding climate and security crises. Discussions focused on national preparations for potential extreme weather impacts linked to Super El Niño, alongside ongoing emergencies caused by severe drought, seasonal flooding, armed conflict, internal displacement, and acute food insecurity. Officials assessed operations at the national emergency center to strengthen contingency planning, as overlapping environmental shocks continue to strain local coping capacities and humanitarian service delivery across vulnerable communities.

Europe.headline: Ukraine/Russia — Moscow Warns UK and France Over Missile Technology Transfers
Europe.body: Russia has threatened potential retaliation against military targets inside and outside Ukraine following statements from Britain and France regarding missile technology transfers to Kyiv. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced that Britain would grant Ukraine access to classified technology to enable domestic production of Storm Shadow long-range cruise missiles, alongside a similar technology supply agreement from France. Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova warned that Western nations are playing with fire. The statements follow reports that the CIA director privately warned the Kremlin against launching attacks on NATO members.

Europe.headline: Myanmar — UN Expert Details Russian, Chinese, and Serbian Weapons Transfers
Europe.body: A report by United Nations independent human rights expert Thomas Andrews states that Russia, China, and Serbia have supplied weapons to Myanmar's military junta since it seized power. According to the findings, Russia and China provided fighter jets that are being used to carry out attacks against civilian populations. Andrews urged the UN Security Council to block weapon flows to the regime, asserting that international suppliers transferred arms with full knowledge that they would be used to commit atrocities against civilians.

Asia-Pacific.headline: Nepal & China — Devastating Himalayan flash floods and secondary outburst risk
Asia-Pacific.body: Devastating flash floods along the Nepal-China border have killed at least 165 people, according to Al Jazeera, while Reuters reports hundreds dead and over 1,000 missing, including more than 600 foreign tourists. The torrent of water, mud, and debris destroyed homes, roads, bridges, and power infrastructure in Nepal. United Nations agencies are delivering emergency aid and coordinating local relief efforts. Meanwhile, Chinese authorities warned Nepal of an additional flood risk along the Bhotekoshi River caused by a river blockage and lake formation upstream on the Lhende River, leading Nepal's disaster agency to advise heightened caution in downstream areas.

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: DRC — Rapidly Spreading Ebola Outbreak
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: An Ebola outbreak driven by the Bundibugyo strain in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo has infected at least 5,605 people and killed 2,683 since May 15, according to CDC and Congolese official data. Health experts warn the rapid transmission rate surpasses the country's 2018–2022 outbreak and outpaces early spread during the 2014–2016 West Africa crisis, with actual casualties estimated to be higher. Meanwhile, the World Health Organization has declared an emergency regarding the outbreak, triggering heightened disease surveillance measures in countries including Nigeria.

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Nepal and Tibet — Deadly Flash Floods and Rising Lake Risk
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: Catastrophic flash floods along the Nepal-Tibet border have obliterated entire villages, sweeping away homes and infrastructure. BBC reports at least 160 people killed, while higher estimates from The Guardian place the death toll at least 359 with more than 1,300 missing. Rescue teams and international aid efforts are struggling to access impacted mountain valleys. Humanitarian concerns are escalating following warnings that a newly formed flood lake at the disaster site is rapidly rising and risks bursting.

escalation_risks.potential_impact: Severe downstream flooding along the Bhotekoshi River, risking further loss of life, displacement, and destruction of remaining emergency access routes.

escalation_risks.trigger: The launch of targeted security operations against gang leader Izo 2's forces following threats to execute hostages.
escalation_risks.potential_impact: Immediate execution of dozens of kidnapped residents and intensified violent clashes causing additional civilian casualties and community displacement.

escalation_risks.trigger: Russian military strikes targeting British or French assets inside or outside Ukraine in response to long-range cruise missile technology transfers.
escalation_risks.potential_impact: A direct military confrontation between Russia and Western nations, escalating the broader regional armed conflict.
